senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; cmp. <cite ref="B00502"><he>בטט</he></cite>  a. deriv.)

units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 5a:6">Snh. 5ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 49:10">Gen. XLIX, 10</cite>) <he>הכא ש׳ והתם מחוקק</he> here (in Babylonia) the rod (the Resh Galutha’s office), there the legislator (the Nasi); <cite ref="Genesis 49:10">ib.</cite> <he>אלו ראשי … בש׳</he> those are the Resh-Galuthas who chastise Israel with the rod; <cite ref="Horayot 11b:3">Hor. 11ᵇ</cite> <he>התם ש׳ וכ׳</he> there (in Babylonia) the rod &c.; a. e.—[Tanḥ. B’midb. 16 <he>הש׳ אינו מספיק</he>, read: <he>השָׂרָף</he>.]

senses.gloss: (cmp. מַטֶּה) tribe. Tanḥ. l. c. למוד הוא הש׳ הזה וכ׳ this tribe (of Levi) is wont to be counted &c.
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 5:8">Num. R. s. 5</cite>, beg. (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 33:18">Ps. XXXIII, 18</cite>) <he>זה שִׁבְטוֹ של לוי וכ׳</he> this means the tribe of Levi whose members sit hoping &c.; <cite ref="Psalms 33:18">ib.</cite> <he>אלו כ״ד … לש׳ לוי</he> those are the twenty-four gifts assigned to the tribe of Levi.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 1:2:2">Y. Ter. I, 40ᵈ</cite> top <he>מפני גזל הש׳</he> because it is an injustice to the tribe (of Levi, giving them unnecessary trouble).

<cite ref="Pesachim 80a:3">Pes. 80ᵃ</cite> <he>ש׳ אחד איקרי קהל</he> one tribe is called a community, v. <cite ref="S00209"><he>קָהָל</he></cite>; <cite ref="Pesachim 80a:2">ib.</cite> <he>אפי׳ ש׳ אחד טמא וכ׳</he> even if one tribe is unclean (and prevented from offering the Passover sacrifice) &c. Y. ib. VII, 34ᶜ <he>ש׳ אחד גורר וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="C01392"><he>גָּרַר</he> I</cite>; a. v. fr.—Pl. <he>שְׁבָטִים</he>.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 98:13">Gen. R. s. 98</cite>; s. 99 end, v. <cite ref="J00268"><he>יָחַד</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 117b:3">B. Bath. 117ᵇ</cite> <he>דילמא לש׳ קאמר לה</he> perhaps the text (<cite ref="Numbers 26:55">Num. XXVI, 55</cite>) means a distribution by tribes (as they were on entering the land)? <cite ref="Shabbat 146a:2">Sabb. 146ᵃ</cite> <he>יעקב הוליד י֞ב ש׳ וכ׳</he> Jacob begat twelve tribes (sons) in whom there was no blemish.
<cite ref="Shabbat 147b:10">Ib. 147ᵇ</cite> <he>עשרת הש׳</he> the ten tribes (the kingdom of Israel).
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 10:3">Snh. X, 3</cite> (<cite ref="Sanhedrin 110b:6">110ᵇ</cite>) <he>עשרת הש׳ אינן וכ׳</he> the ten tribes (carried into exile) are not destined to return; a. fr.
